$comment: Coordinator operations of the executions domain; the rules are in ops.schema.json $comment and contracts/README.md.

delivery_status.description: All projects the caller may see, narrowed to projectIds when given; a repository shows when a project the caller sees, in projectIds and not in excludeProjectIds, lists it.

delivery_history.description: Delivered pull requests and releases with their checks, optionally of one number or release or a time range

delivery_baseline.description: Delivery check durations and failure rates over the last days

delivery_regressions.description: Delivery checks that regressed against the baseline, optionally of one check

execution_differences.description: previous: the earlier execution of the same session.

execution_events.description: Read events in order for a visible agent_run or host_job by executionId. Inspect a pipeline_run with pipeline_get by runId. For a pipeline_step, pass its parent run's ID and find the step in plan.entries. Use pipeline_history to find run IDs by project. For a step's agent or host job events, use the plan entry's execution.nativeExecutionId when present and visible.

execution_status.description: Execution state (preparing, running, waiting, succeeded, failed, cancelled; observation unconfirmed when the host lost track), stop outcome proven|unknown, suggested next action and resume info

executions_abandon.description: Owner or full access: end unfinished agent runs or host jobs no host will finish (ids, reason): failed, problem unknown:abandoned, parent woken, one audit row each

executions_dismiss.description: Owner or full access: take problems of finished executions off Needs you (ids, reason); the problem stays on the record; one audit row each

executions_reconcile.description: Owner or full access: preview or reconcile stuck executions with no live worker process, leaving active runs untouched; writes one audit row each

execution_stop.description: Stop an execution (executionId); returns whether the stop is proven or unknown

db_explain.description: Owner or full access: verify a screen under RLS. Runs the view operation view (contract view: true) with args as you, records each database statement it sends, then runs EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) of each in the same read-only transaction, under row level security as the app reads (20 s timeout per statement). Answers the handler's own time and each distinct statement with its calls, its plan text (planning and execution times) or its error. Never takes SQL from the caller.

executions_list.description: Read executions with optional project/task/session/parent/problem/needsYou filters; projectIds keeps those projects, excludeProjectIds leaves those out ('-' is no project). Fleet's own background calls (systemActor set) are left out unless system is include or only, or parentExecutionId names their parent. For bounded enumeration set limit (1..1000); reply has executions and hasMore, plus nextAfter when more rows exist. Repeat identical filters with after=nextAfter until hasMore=false. Order is seq,id; pages use fresh snapshots. Without limit returns the complete legacy executions wrapper, without paging metadata. after requires limit; inaccessible, unknown or filter-mismatched cursors return 400.

executions_runners.description: CI runners and the executions they ran

hosts_remove.description: Owner, or the holder of the host: remove a host (id, preview). Preview first: running executions, open sessions, artifacts with no other copy; confirm cancels its running work and drops its secret and settings; the record stays for history until system_purge

object_delete.description: Owner only: delete a test project, a Lab experiment, a task or a session with everything that goes with it (kind project|experiment|task|session, id, preview); a task or session a live one depends on is refused with Kept by <reason>. Call preview: true first and read affected (counts per kind, artifact bytes) and running; preview: false stops its running work (stopDetail deleted), revokes run tokens, withdraws open questions, sends worktree teardowns and tombstones it: it leaves every list, detail, search, queue, dispatch and analytics read. One audit row; system_purge removes the rows later

system_purge.description: Owner only: remove tombstoned objects nothing live references (preview, kinds host|project|experiment|task|session, default all): rows, then store objects and spans. Call preview: true first; removed and kept list ids per kind, rows the counts that go with them, retryLater the store/span deletions still pending. A purged project keeps its id reserved

system_changes.description: Drift across repository, active store and hosts: repository-changed and store-only definitions, release version alignment, harness CLI pin drift, and the release-managed components by kind (agent CLIs, host tools): pinned version, the open pin proposal with its stage and Lab trials, and each host's state; the agent environment: connection grants drift, key pools and the sandbox by profile

system_versions.description: Versions of the coordinator, the app and every host's executor

host_diagnose.description: Diagnose a host without SSH or its files (owner or the host's holder): last poll, version, the executor's log tail, outbox and its refused rows, failed transfers, unsettled journal commands, the coordinator's unconfirmed commands, and every queued turn or step with the reason dispatch skipped this host. Asks the host for a fresh report and waits up to wait seconds (default 30, max 60; 0 asks and answers at once); an offline host answers with its latest report and its age.

host_diagnosis.description: A host's latest diagnosis without asking it again (the host detail's Diagnosis section): the same reply as host_diagnose with wait 0. The coordinator asks every online host for a report every few minutes, and host_diagnose asks at once.

host_update_history.description: A host's update history, newest first, one page per request (before: the previous reply's nextCursor): each change of the update result the host reported (version, state, reason, when), the component versions that release pins for the host (cli/codex, tool/node) and those it changed against the release the host last switched to.

hosts_list.description: includeRemoved: also hosts removed by hosts_remove (state removed).

hosts_register.description: Owner only. secretSha256: the sha256 of a secret the host already holds; absent: Fleet mints one.

hosts_update.description: Owner, or the holder for their own host.

pipeline_get.description: Read a visible pipeline run by runId. To inspect a pipeline step, pass its parent run's ID as runId and find the step in plan.entries. If provided, projectId must match the run's project. Use pipeline_history to find run IDs by project.

pipeline_history.description: Page through the project’s runs oldest first. Pass nextCursor as cursor to continue. Use pipeline_get for full run details.

pipeline_rerun.description: Rerun a pipeline run (runId) in mode, optionally from its draft, with a requestId

pipeline_run.description: Run an enabled method from catalogue for the selected project. Omit methodId to use the project recommendation. Idempotent by requestId. If truncated is true, use pipeline_get with the returned id for details.

pipeline_run_create.description: Start a stored pipeline by pipelineId with projectId and a stable requestId; read its runId with pipeline_get.

route_decisions.description: Why an execution (executionId) was routed to its host and account; or, with subscriptionId, the newest 50 decisions since since (epoch ms, default the last 24 h) that skipped that subscription somewhere (J5 model skips carry cause subscription:<id>:model:<model>)

sandbox.$comment: The sandbox every agent profile gets, grouped by harness, mode and network.

AgentEnvironment.$comment: What every future agent gets (Changes › Agent environment): connection grants and key pools, the sandbox by profile, the profile count. Host tools and profile drift are the components and definitions of the same reply.

mode.$comment: Plain words: what a writable run may write, or that it has no sandbox.

network.$comment: The run may use the network (gitNetwork on Codex; Claude's Bash and an unsandboxed run always).

since.$comment: RFC 3339 time or YYYY-MM-DD; default 7 days ago. Pull requests by merge time, runs by creation, releases by publication

number.$comment: one pull request and its merge-queue runs

release.$comment: exact release tag; selects its pull requests regardless of the date window

installsFrom.$comment: host installs and UI on site are recorded from this time on; GitHub keeps no record of them

DeliveryHistoryReply.$comment: The recorded delivery history of the fleet repository (go/coordinator/delivery_history.go), oldest first.

installed.$comment: host id (or coordinator, the PDS18 coordinator part) to when it first ran this release or newer

durations.$comment: ms per stage: pr_ci opened..PR CI done, enqueue ..enqueued, queue ..merge-queue CI done, merge ..merged, release ..published, install ..on the coordinator, ui ..UI on site, lead opened..merged, total opened..on the coordinator (a UI-only release, tag ui-<backend>-v<UI version>: no install, ui_install published..UI on site in place of ui, total opened..UI on site)

queueRemovals.$comment: merge-queue runs that did not succeed

flakes.$comment: removals the pull request landed after without a new commit

DeliveryRun.$comment: One merge_group run of the ci workflow; skipped jobs are left out.

waitMs.$comment: created to started: waiting for a runner

key.$comment: a stage (DeliveryPr durations), run (merge-queue run wall time), job:<name> (job duration) or wait:<name> (runner wait)

DeliveryBaseline.$comment: P50/P90 over a window (nearest rank); a named one is a stored snapshot.

ratio.$comment: a P50 or P90 of the last 24 h this many times the baseline's is a regression (default 1.5)

minSamples.$comment: both windows need this many values (default 5)

minDeltaMs.$comment: and the difference at least this (default 60000)

baseline.$comment: the snapshot name compared with; empty: the 7 days before the last 24 h

days.$comment: trend length in days, default 7, at most 60; the rolling baseline is always 7 days

trend.$comment: stages per UTC day, oldest first

snapshot.$comment: store the rolling 7-day baseline now under this name (replaces one of the same name)

remove.$comment: delete the snapshot of this name

check.$comment: run the check now (full access) instead of returning the last one

DeliveryRegressionsReply.$comment: The last regression check (daily and after each release): the last 24 h against the baseline. Each regression holds one needs-you question (cause problem:delivery:<key>:<metric>) that withdraws itself when the value is back.

firstPr.$comment: the first pull request of the last 24 h over the threshold

lastGoodPr.$comment: the pull request merged just before it

ExecutionsDismissRequest.$comment: Owner or full access: takes execution problems off Needs you (a problem-dismissal record); the problem stays on the record; one setting-change audit row each. An open execution is skipped: abandon it instead.

ExecutionsAbandonRequest.$comment: Owner or full access: ends unfinished agent runs and host jobs that no host will finish (failed, problem unknown:abandoned); one setting-change audit row each.

ExecutionsReconcileRequest.$comment: Owner or full access: preview or reconcile stuck executions with no live worker process, leaving active runs untouched.

state.$comment: The execution's state, or unknown (no agent run or host job).

ExecutionsCiReply.$comment: The Runners screen's CI half for taskqorg/fleet, the last background pass (every FLEET_RUNNERS_CI_TICK_MS, default 1 min, first at start) read through githubRead (cached; keyed through the github connection, else unauthenticated). jobs: in progress and queued. minutesToday: job wall minutes since 00:00 UTC per runner type; runsUncounted: today's runs whose jobs are not read yet (minutes are a lower bound while above 0). runners: self-hosted runners, null without a key (state unknown).

CiJob.$comment: runner: the self-hosted runner's name, else the hosted label (ubuntu-latest). Times in ms.

DiffFile.$comment: state added, removed, unchanged or modified; textChange only for small html and css files.

ExecutionDifferencesRequest.$comment: previous: the earlier execution of the same session.

items.$comment: A stored host event (native data stays raw).

observation.$comment: confirmed or unconfirmed; independent of lifecycle state.

reason.$comment: Why observation is unconfirmed; null when confirmed. Lifecycle state is independent of observation.

resume.$comment: session_resume's reply for the execution's session.

ExecutionStatusReply.$comment: next: the suggested operation (message, session_fork, execution_status or wait_or_steer). stop only after a stop request.

ExecutionStopReply.$comment: The stop command and the stop outcome.

nextAfter.$comment: Present when hasMore is true; pass as after with identical filters.

hasMore.$comment: Present in paged mode, including false on exhaustion; omitted for legacy calls.

handlerMs.$comment: The view's handler, its statements and Go work together, measured while recording.

statements.$comment: In the order first sent; at most 60.

calls.$comment: How many times the handler sent it (with any arguments); the plan is of the first call's arguments.

plan.$comment: EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) text; empty with error.

projectIds.$comment: keep rows of these projects only (the app passes the person's focus, OR-34); '-' is no project

excludeProjectIds.$comment: leave out rows of these projects (the app passes the person's ignored projects while the view names no project, OR-34); '-' is no project (an empty id or null is a 400); applied after projectIds, so a project in both is left out. Agents see every project unless they pass it.

limit.$comment: Opt in to paging: 1..1000 rows. Omit for the legacy complete list.

after.$comment: nextAfter from the preceding page with identical filters; requires limit.

ExecutionsListRequest.$comment: Filters; problem true keeps executions with a problem; needsYou true keeps the problems that still need someone (Needs you): not dismissed, not abandoned or cancelled, no tool calls or steps of a listed run, project still defined. Paging is opt-in with limit (1..1000); repeat identical filters and pass nextAfter as after until hasMore is false. Order is (seq,id). Each page is a fresh read snapshot; concurrent updates can move rows. Unknown, inaccessible or filter-mismatched cursors return 400. Without limit the complete legacy list is returned and nextAfter is omitted. system (default exclude) leaves out Fleet's own background calls (systemActor set), include adds them, only keeps them alone.

ExecutionsRunnersReply.$comment: The Runners screen: executions active or ended in the last 24 hours (newest first, at most 500; pipeline runs and steps left out, their agent and tool runs are listed), and spend since the start of the UTC day and month.

sessionTitle.$comment: The session's stored or generated title, for a run without a task (Live events).

attempt.$comment: Which attempt of its task this run is (its place among the task's executions); null without a task or for grouped tool calls.

RunnerRun.$comment: Tool calls come as one row per caller (id calls:<parent, session or host:id>) with calls and failedCalls; other runs have them null. Times in ms since epoch; resource fields null when not measured. tokens: input + output + cache. cost: CostFigure figures (prices table), empty when nothing was used.

RunnerSpend.$comment: Spend per host and period (today, month: UTC). kind "all": the host's runs, tokens and cost from execution_spend (as spend_summary by host); kind of an execution (today only): that kind's run count, no tokens or cost. measured, wallMs and cpuMs are not summed (0, null).

HostRecord.$comment: A registered host (without its secret hash). harnesses: per harness name whether it is allowed; autoUpdate on, off or an RFC 3339 time; maxConcurrent: owner-configured concurrency limit (null when unset).

stores.$comment: Reporting host checks: reachable, unreachable, mixed, or unknown; never global store health.

toolVersions.$comment: the host tools the host reports (observed null while the host is stale)

slotLimit.$comment: how many runs the host takes at once: slots (maxConcurrent) when set, else the CPU count of a fresh load reading, else null (no limit known)

runs.$comment: the runs (preparing or running) on this host the caller may see, oldest start first; slot tile i shows runs[i] (Live: max(slotLimit, running) tiles; running is counted in the same scope)

HostRow.$comment: One host as the Hosts screen shows it: configured, observed, or both; problems only while it polls; pollError only while its polls fail.

release.$comment: the coordinator's healthy release this decision is about

state.$comment: current: the host runs this release's host part (executor, CLI and tool pins), nothing to install; offered: the poll offers the release; deferred: a normal change waits for an idle host or the daily window

HostUpdatePacing.$comment: How the coordinator paces this host's next install, from its last poll (docs/designs/fleet-host-updates.md section 7); absent before the host's first poll under pacing.

HostProblem.$comment: A host observation problem including edge redirects, production browser readiness and version drift. Route and status describe an edge response when kind is edge-redirect.

HostRun.$comment: One run on a host, in the order slot tiles are filled (go/coordinator/hosts.go hostRuns).

at.$comment: ms since epoch of the host's latest inventory

teardown.$comment: worktrees answered teardown in the latest inventory

unknown.$comment: worktrees with no live session row

leftoverBytes.$comment: bytes of the teardown and unknown worktrees

projectId.$comment: empty for sessions without a project or unknown to the coordinator

load1.$comment: 1-minute load average; CPU load in percent is 100 * load1 / cpus

tmpUsed.$comment: bytes used in /tmp when it is tmpfs (Linux)

top.$comment: the top memory consumers, largest first (docs/designs/fleet-host-cleanup.md#5-readings); pid 0 when the reading came from a heartbeat span

diskFree.$comment: bytes free on the disk of the executor's data directory

at.$comment: ms since epoch of the reading

HostLoadReading.$comment: The host's latest load reading from its polls and heartbeat spans; only while the host polls and the reading is under 2 minutes old.

status.$comment: the HTTP status the coordinator answered the host poll with

reason.$comment: a reason code: the error's reason (pipeline_format_unsupported) or http_<status>; never free text

message.$comment: the error message, cut to 300 characters; may carry data

since.$comment: ms since epoch of the first failed poll in this run of failures (failures less than 5 minutes apart)

at.$comment: ms since epoch of a recent failed poll, rewritten at most once a minute while nothing else changes

HostPollError.$comment: The last failed poll of a host as the coordinator answered it (go/coordinator/host_poll_health.go); cleared by the next successful poll.

HostWriteReply.$comment: secret: only when Fleet minted it (no secretSha256 given); shown once.

SystemVersionsReply.$comment: Installed versions of every Fleet part in one read (go/coordinator/versions.go): the coordinator, the UI the site serves, the gateway when configured, and each host's executor with its update state.

offered.$comment: the healthy release offered to executors; absent: no update offered

UiKind.$comment: bundled: the UI built into the coordinator release; ui: an independently installed UI release

GatewayState.$comment: the gateway's /healthz status (draining: shutting down), or unreachable

behind.$comment: the executor runs a release older than the offered healthy target; null when either release is not comparable

pollError.$comment: only while the host's polls fail (HostRow.pollError)

pollProblem.$comment: true once the host's polls have failed for hostPollProblemAfterMs, the rule that opens its poll problem (go/coordinator/host_poll_health.go): the confirmed failure the version mark tones for; absent otherwise

HostsListRequest.$comment: includeRemoved: also hosts removed by hosts_remove (state removed).

HostsRemoveRequest.$comment: Owner, or the holder for their own host (fleet-system-management.md, Hosts). preview true changes nothing and returns the counts; false removes: running work is cancelled, the secret and settings are dropped, the host record stays as a tombstone (state removed) for history.

PurgeKind.$comment: Tombstoned objects system_purge removes: hosts removed by hosts_remove, projects, experiments, tasks and sessions deleted by object_delete.

PurgeCount.$comment: bytes: stored artifact bytes of the objects (project and experiment). reasons (kept entries): why each id stays.

PurgeReason.$comment: reason: the first live row that keeps the object ("<table>.<column> by <document kind or table> <row id>"), a pending command a live host has not finished ("pending <kind> command <id> on host <host>"), for a host what history still names it, or "deferred: time budget; run system_purge again" (prefix deferred) when this call stopped before reaching it.

SystemPurgeRequest.$comment: Owner only. Removes tombstoned objects (kinds, default all) that no live row references, with every row that goes with them (the reference map in go/coordinator/cleanup.go): a removed host with no execution, session, command, store or artifact copy naming it; a deleted experiment or project whose rows no row outside it names. A purged project keeps its definition row, so its id is never reused. preview true counts them and changes nothing; the confirm recomputes with the same queries, deletes the rows, then the store objects no remaining artifact shares and the ClickHouse spans of the removed executions.

SystemPurgeReply.$comment: more: the call stopped at its time budget (60 s, under the 100 s of the site proxy) with objects left unchecked (deferred, in random order per call); run it again; a preview with more is partial. removed and kept: one entry per requested kind, host first; kept are tombstoned objects a live row still references, they stay. rows: what goes with the removed projects and experiments, per kind. retryLater: store object and span deletions not done yet; the next purge retries them.

ObjectKind.$comment: The object kinds of the reference map (fleet-system-management.md, Archive, delete, purge).

DeleteKind.$comment: Kinds object_delete deletes. A task takes its executions (with their child runs), questions and artifacts; a session takes its executions, messages and questions.

ObjectDeleteRequest.$comment: A task another live task depends on (task_dependency), whose artifacts a live task accepted, or that a live session or task names as its creator stays (409 Kept by); a session that a live session forked or was created from, that created a live task, or whose executions belong to a live task stays too (delete the task first). Owner only (fleet-system-management.md, Archive, delete, purge). preview true changes nothing and returns what goes with the object; both refuse (409) while a live row outside the object keeps one of its objects (another experiment's score citing a trial). false tombstones it with its tasks, executions (and their child runs), sessions, experiments, questions and artifacts: running work is stopped (pipeline runs cancelled, agent runs stopped with stopDetail deleted), run tokens revoked, open questions withdrawn, worktrees of its sessions get a teardown; a project's connections no other project uses are removed as project_archive does. Deleted objects leave every list, detail, search, queue, dispatch and analytics read; system_purge removes their rows later.

ObjectDeleteReply.$comment: affected: per kind, what goes with the object, the object itself included (artifacts with their stored bytes). running: executions not finished, which the confirm stops. teardowns: worktree teardowns the confirm sent.

HostsRemoveReply.$comment: unreplicatedArtifacts: artifacts whose only verified copy is in a store on this host; they become lost on remove.

HostsRegisterRequest.$comment: Owner only. secretSha256: the sha256 of a secret the host already holds; absent: Fleet mints one.

HostsUpdateRequest.$comment: Owner, or the holder for their own host.

PipelineGetReply.$comment: One current-format pipeline plan with actual selected execution references and canonical result.

nextCursor.$comment: Pass as cursor to continue. Absent on the last page.

PipelineRunCreateRequest.$comment: Body of POST /api/pipelines/{id}/runs (pipelineRunCreate) as an operation pipeline_run_create; pipelineId was the URL segment. draft true runs the caller's draft. The request signature includes draft and the content sha.

PipelineRunReply.$comment: One current-format pipeline run. When truncated is true, use pipeline_get with id to read the full plan.

PipelineRunRequest.$comment: Runs the project's method for a capability; files the method reads go in inputs (an artifact saved with artifact_save, or a file on one of the project's files grants by ref). wait false answers the started run at once (follow it with pipeline_get); absent or true waits for it to end. Idempotent by requestId. If truncated is true, use pipeline_get with the returned id for details.

PipelineRunInput.$comment: An input file of pipeline_run, given to every step as example/<path>; path is relative, for example passport.jpg. Exactly one of artifactId (a stored artifact of the project: save the file with artifact_save first) and ref (a file on a ready files grant of the project, which Fleet reads and stores as an artifact before the run is planned).

PipelineRunRef.$comment: A file Fleet reads for pipeline_run: connection is a ready files grant connection of the run's project (for example dam-files); path is the server's own path under a granted folder.

PipelineRunNotify.$comment: A project app's callback: when the run ends Fleet posts {runId, requestId, state, finishedAt} to url, signed with the app's callback secret (X-Fleet-Signature: sha256=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of the body>). Only for an app caller whose callbackOrigins hold the URL's https origin.

items.$comment: A queued message with queued: true and its position (1 is next).

projectIds.$comment: keep rows of these projects only (the app passes the person's focus, OR-34); '-' is no project

excludeProjectIds.$comment: leave out rows of these projects (the app passes the person's ignored projects while the view names no project, OR-34); '-' is no project (an empty id or null is a 400); applied after projectIds, so a project in both is left out. Agents see every project unless they pass it.

DeliveryStatusRequest.$comment: All projects the caller may see, narrowed to projectIds when given; a repository shows when a project the caller sees, in projectIds and not in excludeProjectIds, lists it.

DeliveryStatusReply.$comment: The last GitHub read (go/coordinator/delivery.go). source key: through the github connection; public: unauthenticated REST, the fleet repository only; none: no read yet. landing: pull requests with auto-merge on or in the merge queue, one waiting worker each.

release.$comment: the release tag: v<version>, or ui-<backend>-v<UI version> for a UI-only release, which hosts do not install: installing until the site serves that UI or a newer one, then installed

opened.$comment: when the pull request was opened (RFC 3339)

merged.$comment: when it merged, for merged pull requests

sessionId.$comment: the Fleet session whose worktree branch (<branch prefix>/<session id>) the pull request is from

DeliveryItem.$comment: One pull request or merge request in its current delivery stage; since: when it entered it (RFC 3339). installed and merged are the last 24 hours only.

DeliverySample.$comment: Pull requests per stage of one repository (repo, owner/name) at one read, the last 24 hours; a repository in several projects has one sample per project.

RouteDecisionsRequest.$comment: executionId, or subscriptionId with an optional since (epoch ms).

StopOutcome.$comment: outcome proven (detail stopped or already_finished) or unknown (detail unconfirmed, with the stop command when one exists).

at.$comment: when the head revision was saved (RFC 3339)

experiment.$comment: store-only: the live Lab experiment that names it as a variant; it leaves when the experiment is decided

SystemChangePublish.$comment: The Fleet task that sends the head to the repository (definition_publish), and its latest pull request: the row's progress.

SystemChangeExperiment.$comment: A live Lab experiment whose variants are store-only definitions (SystemChangeDefinition.experiment).

components.$comment: Release-managed components by kind (cli, tool; docs/designs/fleet-host-updates.md): the pinned version, the open proposal and each host's state.

enabled.$comment: false: the release leaves the kind to the hosts (hosts keep their own)

proposal.$comment: absent: no open proposal and none landed in the last day

SystemPinsProposal.$comment: The kind's open pull request automation/<kind>-pins, or the one merged in the last day (landed), as the delivery pass last read it.

blocked.$comment: stage blocked: why GitHub holds the qualified proposal, such as an approving review a ruleset requires

trials.$comment: the Lab experiment pins:<kind>:<head sha>; absent before it starts

pinned.$comment: this release's version for linux-amd64 (darwin-arm64 when only that is pinned)

proposed.$comment: the proposal's version when it changes this component

failures.$comment: the proposal's failed trials of this component

state.$comment: own: the kind is not pinned and the host keeps its own; unknown: the host reports no version; failing: the pinned version fails clearly more on this host than its other versions (the pin watch)

pinned.$comment: the version this release pins for the host's target; absent when it pins none

fresh.$comment: the report arrived after this request asked for it

coordinatorCommands.$comment: commands of open work (or of no execution) the coordinator holds for this host that it has not confirmed (oldest first, at most 50)

waiting.$comment: queued agent runs (turns and steps) no host took yet, with this host's skip reason from the latest dispatch decision (null: no decision names this host)

before.$comment: Page: entries with seq below this (the previous reply's nextCursor).

components.$comment: the versions the release pins for the host's target; empty when unknown

brought.$comment: the components whose version differs from the release the host last switched to
